answer: A karst valley holds one spring pool per agent, each rim marked by a single opal chip set in stone. To claim a pool, the agent writes a fourteen-line sonnet recording the flow, the chip color, and the date, then reads it aloud while a keeper measures the flow with a bucket and a watch. A second keeper returns a week later, measures again and checks the flow against the sonnet line by line. A thousand fake names need a thousand sonnets, a thousand opal chips, and a thousand pools measured twice, and no forger writes a thousand true sonnets in a week.
